source: Remodeling Magazine / Zonda / JLC 2025 Cost vs. Value Report
notes: Original source at remodeling.hw.net and jlconline.com blocked by Cloudflare (403)
Data compiled from secondary sources: customcraftdbr.com, dadimprovement.com, newagedesignandbuild.com
Report covers 28 remodeling projects across 119 US markets
Exterior projects consistently outperform interior projects for ROI
New in 2025: backup generators, ADUs, basement remodels, rooftop solar

top_projects_by_roi.note: Wide variance in ROI calculation methods across secondary sources
New category for 2025; more relevant in storm-prone areas

major_kitchen_remodel_midrange.note: Returns less than 50% — buyers prefer to customize

basement_remodel.note: New category for 2025; national avg ROI 71% per JLC

adu_accessory_dwelling_unit.note: New for 2025; returns vary widely by market; CA loosened ADU rules

rooftop_solar.note: New for 2025; payback depends on local utility rates and incentives

key_insights: 8 of top 10 projects are exterior improvements
Curb appeal projects consistently outperform interior remodels
Minor kitchen remodels return 2-3x more than major gut renovations
Luxury/upscale upgrades rarely recoup full cost at resale
Exterior taste is universal; interior taste is personal — buyers prefer to customize interiors
Small targeted improvements often beat big renovations for ROI
Energy efficiency upgrades add both resale value and utility savings
Universal Design (accessibility) bathroom remodels are a growing trend
roi_note: IMPORTANT: Different sources cite different ROI figures for the same projects. This is because some calculate ROI as (Resale Value / Cost) while others calculate Cost Recouped as (Resale Value / Cost × 100%). The NewAge source appears to use resale_value/cost ratio (267% = $12,507/$4,672) while DadImprovement uses a different methodology. Both are from the same underlying report.
